feedback.problem: The length of a curve $y=f(x)$ is given by ${\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{4x+4}}\,\text{d}x.$ Which of the following could be  an equation for this curve?
feedback.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We're given that 

$$
L={\int }_{0}^{4}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{4x+4}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Comparing the above with the arc length formula, we see that we must have

$$
[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}=\frac{1}{4x+4}\,⟹\,{f}^{′}(x)=\pm \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+1}}.
$$

Integrating the above equation with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\pm \int \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+1}}\text{ d}x \\  & =\pm \sqrt{x+1}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given options, the only one that has the required form is $y=\sqrt{x+1}+1.$
